title: Make peer-channel port selection honor wildcard daemon listeners
goal: Prevent parallel integration tests from selecting a peer-channel block already occupied on a non-loopback interface
limitations: The probe remains a race with an unrelated process binding after the check; daemon startup retry behavior remains responsible for that race.

results.why: peer_channel_hub checked only loopback while daemon tests can bind the same contract on all interfaces, so parallel runs could select an occupied block.
results.change: The free-block probe now checks both wildcard and loopback TCP/UDP bindings, matching the host-wide daemon contract.
results.tests: cargo fmt --all --check: exit 0; cargo test --offline --locked -p susi --test peer_channel_hub -- --nocapture: 2 passed, 0 failed; peer_channel_hub and host_only_privacy run concurrently: 2/2 passed in each process; exact acceptance rerun on ebfed31f6: 2 passed, 0 failed
results.integrated: The feature commits are present on origin/main through the 708938c7e landing and the current origin/main ebfed31f6; strict workspace clippy, lean_core_ceilings, and the exact peer-channel acceptance all pass on the current native Linux tree.
